reuse.why: Reuses isTrackingBudget, getCategoryAverage, getBudgetData, setBudget and the shared extractTagsFromText for the #fixed tag; the templated-category query is a small new SQL check next to goal-template's private getTemplates.

duplication.why: The repeated income/hidden checks, the three copies of the visible-categories SQL and the average sign flip are consolidated into isMonthFillCategory, getMonthFillCategories and averageToBudgetAmount; only copyPreviousMonth re-composes the filter with managedIds itself.

placement.why: The selection and sign helpers live in budget/actions.ts beside the month-wide actions that use them, and the new action is registered in budget/app.ts next to its siblings.

scope.why: Every edit serves one of the steps (shared definition, exclusions, new action, #fixed groups, includeHiddenCategories) plus tests and a release note.

maintainability.why: A future rule change lands in one place for most actions, with the ungrouped-category inconsistency named as an explicit scope; copyPreviousMonth's separate composition and reusing averageToBudgetAmount for last-month spending are small wrinkles.

bypasses_abstraction.where: copyPreviousMonth calls isMonthFillCategory and getManagedCategoryIds separately instead of a single shared selection, so it composes the exclusion rule itself

disguised_duplication.where: The only repeat is copyPreviousMonth's isMonthFillCategory && !managedIds.has(...) composition, which is visible rather than disguised

abstraction_drift.where: isMonthFillCategory/getMonthFillCategories gained the scope and includeHiddenCategories parameters with a branch for each; copyPreviousMonth bypasses getMonthFillCategories and joins the managed-id exclusion itself
